Dioscorus was the name of his father and his mother’s name was Euphemia and they raised him with a Christian upbringing. He learned the church subjects in the village school (el-Kutab). The signs of holiness became evident in him since his young age. He was merciful to the poor, and kind to the needy.

When the people recognized his many virtues, they brought him to the bishop who ordained him a priest for the church of the village. During the ordination the people present heard a voice saying; “Axios...Axios...Axios” (that is to say, Worthy). He shepherded his flock with sincerity and uprightness. The sweet aroma of his demeanor spread in every place and St. Julius of Aqfahs (el-akfehasi) desired to see him. He came to him with some of his men and received his blessing. He took him to his village Aqfahs where he stayed for few days then returned to his hometown.

Persecution intensified against the Christians and Arianus the governor came to Elfant to force the people to worship the idols. When Abba Kloag knew of his coming, he gathered his flock in the church and celebrated the Divine Liturgy. He preached them to be steadfast in the faith till the last breath. Then he went to Arianus and confessed the Lord Christ before him. Arianus seized him and tried to entice him with high ranking positions but the saint refused. Then he threatened him with the severest kinds of torture but the saint did not fear the tortures and was steadfast in his Orthodox faith.

The Governor severely tormented him then took him to Ahnasia where he retried him and tortured him again. However the angel of the Lord strengthened and encouraged him and he wrought some miracles in prison. The Governor ordered to take him back to his hometown and to behead him there thus he received the crown of martyrdom. The church that bears his name in Elfant still has his body in a reliquary.

The blessing of the prayers of the saint aba Kloag be with us all. Amen.
05-20.title: The Martyrdom of Anba Kloag (Bagoug), the Priest

05-20.html:
On this day also was the martyrdom of St. Behna (Bahnou).

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
05-20.title: The Martyrdom of St. Behna (Bahnou)

05-20.html:
This day also marks the commemoration of the consecration of the church of St. John "El-Kokhy" in the city of Rome. He was known as the owner of the Golden Bible. His body was relocated to it from Constantinople. The account of his departure is recorded under the 16th day of the month of Epep.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God forever. Amen.
05-20.title: The Commemoration of the Consecration of the Church of St. John, the Owner of the Golden Gospel

05-21.html:
On this day of the year 48 A.D. the pure Virgin St. Mary, the Mother of God, departed. After the ascension of our Lord Jesus Christ to heaven, she lived in the house of St. John the beloved for 15 years. She visited the holy sepulcher often to pray there. She was informed by the Holy Spirit about the time of her departure, and she rejoiced. Our fathers the apostles gathered around her and our lady the Virgin blessed them. Then the Lord Jesus Christ came in person surrounded by His holy angels. The Lord received her pure spirit and ascended with it to heaven.

The apostles prepared her pure body in a fitting manner, and carried it to Gethsemane to be entombed there. On their way, one of the Jews tried to prevent them from doing so and seized the coffin. His arms were separated instantly from his body and they remained attached to the coffin. He regretted his evil deed and wept bitterly. Through the supplications of the holy apostles, his arms were re-attached to his body again. He believed immediately in the Lord Jesus. The apostles continued their procession until they arrived to Gethsemane where they buried her with great veneration.

The years of her life on earth were about sixty years.

Her holy intercession and blessings be with us all. Amen.
05-21.title: The Departure of the Virgin St. Mary, the Mother of God

05-21.html:
On this day also of the year 229 of the martyrs (513 A.D.), the righteous St. Hilaria, the daughter of Emperor Zeno, departed. This saint was born in the later part of the fifth century. Emperor Zeno raised Hilaria and her sister Thaopesta with a true Christian upbringing.

Hilaria was inclined to a life of virginity and longed for monasticism. She could not go to a convent nearby Constantinople for she knew that they will not accept her for their fear of her father. She thought and prayed often for the Lord to guide her life. She put on the attire of men and embarked on a ship to Alexandria.

Then she went to the wilderness of Shiheet and arrived to the monastery of St. Macarius the great. She met the Holy Father Anba Pemwah. She told him about her life story and her desire to become a monk. He accepted her as a monk by the name, Hilary. He placed her in a cave far from the monastery where she dwelt for 15 years in austere ascetic worship. He visited her from time to time. She only came to the monastery to partake of the Holy Mysteries. Since she did not grow a beard they called her "Hilary, the eunuch".

Meanwhile, her younger sister Thaopesta became possessed with an unclean spirit. Her father sent her to the desert for the fathers the monks of the wilderness of Shiheet to pray for her.

When she arrived to the monastery the monks prayed for her for many days but she was not healed. Finally they handed her to the monk Hilary the eunuch to pray for her healing. St. Hilary knew that she was her sister but her sister did not recognize her. The Monk Hilary prayed for her fervently until she was healed. St. Hilaria took her to the elders and said to them, "Through your prayers, God has granted her healing."

The elders sent Thaopesta back to the Emperor who rejoiced to her safe return. Her father asked her about her stay in Shiheet and how she was healed. She said that the saint who healed her with his prayers embraced and kissed her often. The emperor was not comfortable about the behavior of the monk Hilary toward his daughter. He sent to the elders of the wilderness to send him St. Hilary to bless the kingdom. After a great effort, St. Hilaria went to the emperor who had a private meeting with Hilaria together with the Empress. They asked "him", "How could you embrace and kiss the princess?" Then Hilaria asked them to bring the Bible and to make a solemn oath not to hinder "him" from going back to the wilderness after telling them the truth.” After they promised him, he told them, "I am your daughter Hilaria." The Emperor and the Empress greatly rejoiced along with everyone in the royal palace.

She remained in the palace for a month, then she wanted to return to Scetis, and when her parents refused, she reminded them of their oath. Then the Emperor wrote to the governor of Egypt, demanding him to send a large quantity of wheat and oil and all that the monks needed on an annual basis. The Emperor also was greatly interested in building in the wilderness. He built a huge fortress in the monastery of St. Macarius that still exists till present time.

After the return of St. Hilaria to the wilderness, she lived for 12 years persevering in asceticism and worship. When she finished her good endeavor, she delivered her pure soul. The monks prayed over her and buried her with great veneration.

The blessing of her prayers be with us all and glory be to our God forever. Amen
05-21.title: The Departure of St. Hilaria, the Daughter of Emperor Zeno

05-22.html:
On this day of the year 72 of the martyrs (356 A.D.), the great saint Anba Anthony, the star of the wilderness, and the father of all monks, departed.

He was born in the year 251 A.D. in the city of Qiman El-Arous, to rich parents who loved the church and the poor. They raised him up in the fear of the Lord.

His father died and he stood before his body contemplating about the vanity of the world and his heart burned with desire for the eternal life and said; “Where is your ambition, great determination and your eagerness to collect money. I see that everything had become futile and you left it behind. If you had no choice in leaving, I am not surprised at that but I would be surprised about me if I do as you have done.” He also contemplated about the deeds of the fathers the apostles and how they have left all and followed the Savior. And how the people sold their possessions and brought the proceeds and laid them at the apostles’ feet and they distributed to each as anyone had need.

One day he went to the church as he was used to, and he heard the words of Christ in the Gospel, saying, "If you want to be perfect, go, sell what you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasures in heaven; and come, follow Me." (Matthew 19:21) This verse had a profound effect on his heart.

He sold all what he owned, gave to his sister her portion and placed her in a house of virgins (convent). He distributed his portion to the poor and the churches. He went outside the village and dwelt in a small hut beside the Nile. He visited the nearby hermits to learn from everyone the virtue that he was famous for. After a while he crossed the Nile and dwelt in an ancient Pharaonic tomb beside a fig tree on the eastern bank of the Nile. There he faced a fierce warfare from the devil. They had beaten him severely to the point of losing his consciousness and speech. His friends carried him to the church until he started to recover; he decided to go back to his place of worship.

Later on he went deeply in the eastern desert until he found a spring of water. He dwelt beside it in a cave. He persevered in fasting, worship and resisting the devil’s warfare. The Lord supported him to overcome them. The saint went on living there for twenty years and many gathered around him to be discipled at his hands and others came seeking healing from their sicknesses. The saint went out to meet them and many benefited from his guidance and advices and the Lord performed on his hands signs and many healings. Many became his disciples and dwelt in caves around his cave and he became a father and guide for them. By that he founded the first monastic institution in the world so Antonios was rightly called the father of all monks.

He went down to Alexandria twice; the first was in the year 311 A.D. during the persecution of Maximinus Caesar to encourage the believers to steadfast in the faith. He visited the prisoners to encourage them. The second was in the year 355 A.D. to defend the orthodox faith and to stand beside the Holy Father Pope Athanasius the Apostolic against the Arians.

Emperors respected him and everyone honored him. One time some philosophers came to debate him and they marveled at his knowledge and his instinctive intelligence. When the report of his holiness reached Emperor Constantine, he wrote him a letter expressing his great desire to see him, asking for his prayers for his sake and for the sake of the empire. The saint replied by an epistle, blessing him and asking for the peace of the empire and the church and commended him in it with whatever important for his own salvation and the success of his kingdom.

When the departure of the saint Anba Paula the first anchorite, Anba Antonios went to him with divine providence, shrouded the body, then prayed over him and buried the saint.

St. Macarius visited Anba Antonios who dressed him with the monastic garb then Anba Macarius returned to the wilderness of Shiheet and established monasticism there. In the later days of Anba Antonios, he had many disciples in different parts of Egypt, as Shiheet, Nitria, Naklon mount in el-Fayyom. He personally visited them at times and also with his epistles which he had twenty in this respect.

When he finished his good strife, he gathered his children and commended them to steadfast in the monastic strife. He also asked them to give his staff to St. Macarius, to give the sheepskin to St. Athanasius, and his sheepskin cloak to Anba Serapion his disciple. He commanded his disciple to hide his body after his departure. He stretched himself on the ground and delivered up his spirit in the hand of the Lord whom he loved, in a good old age. He went to the place of eternal repose and his age at the time of his departure was 105 years old.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
05-22.title: The Departure of the Great Saint Anba Anthony (Antonius) the Father of all Monks

05-23.html:
On this day, of the year 97 A.D., St. Timothy the apostle, the disciple of St. Paul and bishop of Ephesus, was martyred. This saint was born in the city of Lystra in Asia Minor, to a Greek father and a Jewish mother. His mother raised him up on a life of godliness, faith and studying the Holy Scriptures. St. Paul said, “When I call to remembrance the genuine faith that in you, which dwelt first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and I am persuaded is in you also.” And he also said, “and that from childhood you have known the Holy Scriptures, which are able to make you wise for salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus.”

St. Timothy believed and was baptized at the hands of the apostle St. Paul and became his disciple. He accompanied him in most of his missionary journeys. He ordained him a bishop for Ephesus when he saw him growing in faith. He wrote him two epistles, the first in the year 64 A.D explaining to him his pastoral duties and some ecclesiastical ordinances. The second was in the year 67 A.D. urging him to strive for the sake of keeping the faith.

For his intense pastoral activities, he attracted many of the pagans to Christianity. The wicked of the Jews and the heathen rose against him and beat him severely with sticks and rods until he delivered his spirit in Ephesus thus he received the crown of martyrdom. The faithful took his pure body and buried him with great veneration.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
05-23.title: The Martyrdom of St. Timothy the Apostle

05-23.html:
On this day also of the year 1577 of the martyrs (1861 A.D.) the Holy Father Pope Kyrillos IV (Cyril), 110th Patriarch of Alexandria, departed. He is known as the father of reformation. He was born in the town of Sawamaa Sharq, district of Akhmeem in the year 1816 A.D. His father cared greatly to teach him the church subjects. He grew loving godliness and piety. He longed for the monastic life so he went to the monastery of St. Anthony, and became a monk by the name of Daoud el-Antony.

When the fame of his knowledge and virtues became well known, Pope Peter el-Gawly (109th Patriarch) ordained him a priest and appointed him the abbot of the monastery. He managed the monastery well and cared for educating the monks. Pope Peter (Petros) el-Gawly sent him to Ethiopia to settle a dispute between the metropolitan and the people.

While he was in Ethiopia, Pope Peter el-Gawly departed in the year 1852 A.D. so he returned to Egypt. After a dispute for one year on choosing a Patriarch for the church, the bishops consecrated the monk Fr. Daoud el-Antony a general metropolitan in April 1853 A.D. by the name; Anba Kyrollos. When he managed the affairs of the church well, they enthroned him Patriarch in the year 1854 A.D.

He devoted a great effort in spreading education, for he established schools for boys and girls. He also paid great attention to the teaching of the Coptic language and the church hymns. He also bought a printing press to publish the church books. He also renovated the great St. Mark church in Azbakyah, Cairo. In general he greatly cared for all the affairs of the church. He consecrated some bishops and went to Ethiopia to visit the church there.

After a great and hard endeavor, he reposed in the Lord. The whole Coptic nation grieved for him and was buried in St. Mark church in Cairo. He sat on St. Mark throne for about seven years and because of his many accomplishments the church called him the father of reformation (Abi el-Eslah).

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
05-23.title: The Departure of Pope Cyril (Kyrillos) IV, 110th Patriarch of Alexandria

05-24.html:
On this day, St. Mary the ascetic, and the shut-in, departed. This saint was born in Alexandria to wealthy Christian parents. They raised her up with a Christian upbringing.

Many of the sons of the noble men in the city asked to marry her, but she declined.

When her parents departed, she distributed all what they had left among the poor and the needy. Then she went and became a nun in one of the convents nearby the City of Alexandria. She exerted herself in much worship for 15 years, then she put on the holy Eskeem, and her clothes were made of hair. Later on she took the permission of the abbess to shut herself in her cell. She shut the door on her, and opened a small window to receive her spiritual and physical needs. She fasted two days at a time and broke her fast on dried bread. During the holy fast (Lent), she broke her fast every three days. And she remained as such in her cell for 22 years.

On the day of the honorable Theophany feast she asked for a little of the Lakkan water. She washed her hands and feet, and then she partook of the Holy Mysteries. Shortly after she became ill and she called for the abbess and all the nuns, bade them farewell, then departed in peace. They carried her to the church, prayed over her, and then placed her with the bodies of the holy virgins.

The blessing of her prayers be with us all. Amen.
05-24.title: The Departure of St. Mary the Ascetic (The Shut-In)

05-24.html:
On this day also of the year 20 of the martyrs (304 A.D.), St. Bisada (Psate, Ibsadeh), the priest, was martyred. His mother, who was the daughter of one of the pagan priests, was from Eh-Reet, but she believed in the Lord Christ. When the son of a pagan priest asked her to marry him, she escaped to El-Kais where she married a Christian farmer. God gave her this saint and she called him Bisada.

They brought him up in the fear of God and in keeping of His Commandments. When he was twenty years old, his father departed and left him a great wealth. St. Bisada gave alms from this wealth to the poor, and increased in worship and godliness so they ordained him a priest.

When Emperor Diocletian renounced the faith, a voice came to St. Bisada from heaven saying, "Why is this slacking and the crown is ready?" Immediately, he rushed and came before the Governor and confessed his faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. The Governor ordered to torture him by scourging with whips and pins, pulling out his nails then dipping his fingers in vinegar and lime. But the Lord supported and healed him. When the Governor became weary of torturing him, he chained him and sent him to El-Fayyom.

There he raised a child from the dead that a large stone had fallen on him. Before the Governor of el-Fayyom he confessed again his upright Christian faith. The Governor tortured him severely but the Lord strengthened, and raised him up well. When the Governor became weary of him, he sent him to Armanius the Governor of Alexandria. He confessed his faith before him for a third time. He ordered to behead him and he received the crown of martyrdom.

St. Julius El-Akfehasi took his body and sent it to Ah-Reet where he was buried with great veneration. The Lord had manifested many miracles from his body.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
05-24.title: The Martyrdom of Anba Bisada the Priest

05-25.html:
On this day, St. Peter of Scetis, the ascetic, departed. He was at first a tax collector, who was hard hearted and merciless to the poor.

One day a poor man came to earnestly ask him for a charity but he refused to give him anything. It happened that his servant arrived at that same time bringing to him his food. He took a loaf of bread and hit the poor man with it on his head, not as an act of mercy, but for the poor man not to return to him again.

That same night, he saw a vision in his sleep, as though he was in the last day, where the scale of justice was erected, and the devils came and put his sins and his injustices in the left pan of the scale. Then a group of luminous angels came and stood beside the right pan of the scale. They appeared perplexed, for they did not find any good deeds to put in the pan. One of them came forward, and put the loaf of bread with which he hit the head of the poor man and said, "There is nothing for this man except this loaf of bread."

Peter woke up from his sleep trembling and terrified. He started to rebuke himself for his cruelty and injustice. He sold all his possessions and gave all his money to the poor and needy. When nothing was left to donate to the poor he sold himself as a slave, and paid the price to the poor.

When his fame became well known he fled to the wilderness of Shiheet where he became a monk. He lived an ascetic life with great devotion and good repute that made him worthy to know the day of his departure. He called the monks and bade them farewell, and departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
05-25.title: The Departure of St. Peter of Scetis (the Ascetic)

05-25.html:
On this day also, was the martyrdom of St. Askala (Asela). This saint was brought up in the region of Ansena. In one of the visits of Arianus the governor of Ansena to his home town, summoned him and commanded the saint to raise incense to the idols. He held fast to his faith with courage and determination.

The Governor ordered to tie him to a horse and drag him through the streets of the city. His body was torn into pieces and his flesh was scattered everywhere. The Governor then ordered to direct torches of fire to his sides and stomach however the Lord healed and comforted him.

Arianus embarked on a ship to cross the Nile and took Askala with him. On board of the ship, Askala prayed to God to perform a sign to glorify His name before Arianus. Immediately the ship stopped in the middle of the river, the soldiers tried to move the boat but they could not. Arianus asked Askala to pray to his God for the boat to move. When he prayed immediately the boat moved. However the Governor hardened his heart, and tied a huge rock to his neck and threw him into the Nile and he delivered his pure spirit in the hand of the Lord and received the crown of martyrdom.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
05-25.title: The Martyrdom of St. Askala (Asela)

05-26.html:
On this day of the year 160 of the martyrs (444 A.D.), the forty-nine elders of Shiheet, Martinos (Martin), the envoy of the Emperor, and his son, were martyred.

Emperor Theodosius the Less did not have a son. He sent to the elders of Shiheet an envoy called Martinos asking them to pray to God to grant him a son. They informed him that the Lord did not will for him to have a son lest he would participate with the heretics after him.

Martinos had a son named Zius who accompanied him on his visit to the elders in order to receive their blessings.

After consulting with the elders he wanted to return to his country, however the Berbers attacked the wilderness. One of the elders asked the rest of the fathers to flee to the fortress from the Berbers and whoever would like to become a martyr, let him remain with him. Forty-eight elders stood beside him and were slaughtered by the Berbers and received the crowns of martyrdom.

Martinos and his son were in hiding. The son looked up and saw the angels placing luminous crowns on the heads of the martyred elders. He said to his father, "I shall go to receive a crown." His father replied, "And I also shall go with you.” Immediately they revealed themselves to the Berbers. They were killed and received the crowns of martyrdom.

After the Berbers had gone, the monks who were hiding in the fortress came down, took the bodies of the martyred elders with great veneration, and placed them in a cave outside the monastery.

When the attacks of the Berbers were repeated, the monks relocated the pure bodies, and built for them a church inside the monastery of St. Macarius the great which was consecrated by Pope Theodosius I, 33rd Patriarch, year 528 A.D.

After a long time had passed, the church building deteriorated, and they moved them to one of the cells until the time of Ibrahim El-Gohary, who built a church for them in the year 1782 A.D. inside the monastery and the pure bodies were relocated to it and was called the church of the elders.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all. Amen.
05-26.title: The Martyrdom of the Forty-Nine Saints, the Elders of Shiheet (Scetis)

05-26.html:
Today also was the martyrdom of St. Bagoush. He was a wealthy man loving to the poor and the needy. When Diocletian incited the persecution against the Christians, Michael the Archangel appeared to him and called upon him to confess the Lord Christ before the Governor.

He distributed all his possessions to the poor and went to the Governor to declare his faith. The Governor befriended him to persuade him to change his conviction but he was steadfast in his faith, so he imprisoned him.

When his mother heard, she came and blamed him for leaving her behind without participating in the crown of martyrdom. She remained with him all night long praying to God to grant them the crown of martyrdom. In the next morning, the Governor summoned St. Bagoush, and his mother walked beside him declaring her faith so the Governor ordered to behead her.

As for the Saint, he was tormented with many tortures and finally ordered to behead him thus he received the crown of martyrdom and that was in the village of Tima, Souhag governorate.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
05-26.title: The Martyrdom of St. Bagoush

05-26.html:
On this day also of the year 292 of the martyrs (576 A.D.) St. Anastasia departed. She was from a noble wealthy family in the city of Constantinople. She was of dazzling beauty and had a great moral character.

Emperor Justin, who was still married to Empress Theodora, wanted to marry her. She refused and went to his wife to inform her. The Empress assisted her to flee to Egypt aboard a private ship. She built for her a convent nearby the city of Alexandria.

St. Severus sent her spiritual epistles to comfort her.

The Emperor continued to pursue her in every place to marry her. She put on the attire of men and called herself Anastasy and went to the wilderness of Shiheet. She met with Anba Daniel, the hegumen of the wilderness, and revealed her story to him. He accepted her and chose for Anastasia a cave in the inner wilderness. She lived there and that was in the year 548 A.D. She lived for 28 years in that cave without anyone knowing anything about her. Anba Daniel sent to her his disciple weekly with water and food without seeing her.

She used to write her thoughts on pieces of pottery, and she left them at the door of her cave. The disciple brought the pieces of pottery to Anba Daniel without reading them.

One day he brought a piece of pottery to St. Daniel who wept when he read it. He said to his disciple, "Let us go to the hermit." They went to her cave and found her with severe fever and she asked Anba Daniel, “For the sake of God, do not shroud me but bury me with my clothes,” then she prayed and departed in peace. A sweet aroma of incense filled the cave. The disciple noticed that she was a woman and he marveled in silence. After they had buried her, they returned to their place. The disciple asked his teacher to tell him about her account and Anba Daniel told him her life story.

The blessing of her prayers be with us all and glory be to our God forever. Amen
05-26.title: The Departure of St. Anastasia

05-27.html:
On this day the church celebrates the commemoration of the honorable Archangel Suriel. He is one of the seven Archangels and one of the seven Spirits who are before the throne of God. They are from heaven but they are sent forth to minister to the sons of men for, “the angel of the Lord encamps all around those who fear Him, and delivers them.” “Are they not all ministering spirits sent forth to minister for those who will inherit salvation.”

God created them luminous spirits that have translucent nature that can behold God but only as much as they can tolerate.

The name Suriel means the trumpet of God. Archangel Suriel shall sound the trumpet in the last day when God will send His angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they will gather together His elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.

St. John Chrysostom built for him a splendid church in Constantinople. He consecrated it in his name on the 27th day of the month of Tobe and many miracles had taken place through his intercession.

The blessing of his intercession be with us all. Amen.
05-27.title: The Commemoration of the Honorable Archangel Suriel

05-27.html:
On this day also of the year 20 of the martyrs (304 A.D.) St. Abe-Fam (Bifam or Phoebammon), the Soldier, was martyred. This Saint was born in Oseem (Awsim) to wealthy Christian parents.

They raised him up with a Christian upbringing. He grew up in the fear of the Lord, merciful to the poor and diligent in his prayers and fasting. His parents proposed for him to get married, but he did not accept.

When Emperor Diocletian apostatized and declared the persecution against the Christians, the Saint came before the Governor of the region and confessed the Lord Christ and he extensively tortured him.

It happened that Arianus the governor of Ansena was present in Oseem so he took the Saint with him to Kaw. There he tied him to the tail of a horse and went about with him in the entire city. Then the Governor ordered to squeeze him in the Hinbazeen; however the Lord healed and strengthened him.

Later on Arianus ordered to tie a rock to his neck and to throw him into the river. The Lord sent His angel and saved him from drowning. The Governor became furious and ordered to place the Saint in the fiery furnace but the fire did not harm him and was like cool dew. Finally the Governor ordered to behead him thus he received the crown of martyrdom.

Some of the believers took his pure body, shrouded, and buried him with great veneration in the city of Tima. A church was built after his name and many signs and miracles were manifested from his body.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
05-27.title: The Martyrdom of St. Abe-Fam the Soldier (St. Phoebammon)

05-27.html:
Today also of the year 21 of the martyrs (305 A.D.) was the martyrdom of St. Serapion. This Saint was born in the City of Binosa (Babousah), a town of Lower Egypt, to wealthy Christian parents. He grew to be loving and charitable to the poor and needy.

He heard about the torture of the Christians in Alexandria. He went along with a friend called Theodore (Tadros) and one of the shepherds of his sheep called Thomas to Alexandria. They all came before the Governor Armanius and confessed the Lord Christ. The Governor ordered to imprison them.

He tormented them by squeezing with the Hinbazeen, casting them in boiling tar, crucifying and throwing arrows at them. However the angel of the Lord healed them from all these tortures strengthened and comforted them.

When the Governor became weary, he ordered the commander of his soldiers whose name was Orion to behead St. Serapion thus he received the crown of martyrdom.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
05-27.title: The Martyrdom of St. Serapion

05-27.html:
On this day also, the church celebrates the commemoration of the translocation of the relics of St. Timothy bishop of Ephesus and the disciple of the apostle St. Paul, from the City of Ephesus to Constantinople by the order of Emperor Constantine the great.

They placed his relics with great veneration in the church of the holy fathers the apostles. The account of the martyrdom of St. Timothy is recorded under the 23rd of Tobe.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
05-27.title: The Translocation of the Relics of St. Timothy the Apostle

05-28.html:
On this day of the year 21 of the martyrs (305 A.D.) St. Kaou, the ascetic, was martyred. This Saint was born in the city of Dimoshah (Bamway, Bimay) one of the cities of el-Fayyom in the later part of the third century. He loved to read and contemplate in the Holy Scriptures. He went and dwelt in a cave in the desert of el-Fayyom.

When persecution was incited against the Christians, the angel of the Lord appeared to him in a vision and told him, "Why you are sitting here and the crowns are prepared for the martyrs. Rise and go to el-Lahoon and there confess the Name of the Lord Christ.” Immediately he rose up and went to the city where he found the envoy of the Governor who marveled at his white hair and fair look. He honored him and took out an idol made of gold and decorated with precious stones, and said to the saint, "This is the gift of the Emperor to the Governor of Ansena."

The saint took it in his hand and admired its wonderful workmanship. Then he cast it to the ground and smashed it. The envoy of the Emperor became very angry and ordered him bound. He took him along to the Governor of Ansena and told him what St. Kaou had done. The Governor tormented him by scourging and squeezing by the Hinbazeen. Then he sent him to the Governor of Bahnasa, who in turn hit him with iron hammers and flogged him until his flesh was torn. Then tied red hot iron rods to his body however the Lord Jesus healed and saved him.

When the Governor was helpless, he ordered to behead him with the sword so he received the crown of martyrdom. Some of the believers took his body, shrouded him with great veneration and buried him in the place where he used to worship.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
05-28.title: The Martyrdom of the Saint Anba Kaou

05-28.html:
On this day also of the year 25 of the martyrs (309 A.D.) St. Clement, bishop of Angora, was martyred. This Saint was born in Angora in the year 257 A.D. His heathen father died when he was a suckling infant and his Christian mother took care of raising him and feeding him the milk of faith. He loved the poor and the needy and cared for their spiritual and physical needs. Because of his remarkable growth in virtue, they ordained him deacon and he increased in piety and asceticism. Accordingly he was ordained a priest then he became later on bishop for Angora. He struggled for the sake of his flock with a giving love and rigorous zeal.

The fame of this Saint spread out until it reached Emperor Diocletian who ordered the Governor of Galatia to seize him. He offered him to worship the idols but he refused. He ordered to torture him, tear his flesh with iron hooks and stoned then was cast in prison.

The Governor became helpless in torturing the Saint. He sent him to the Emperor who befriended him and tried often for him to deny his faith. When he could not change his conviction he ordered to tear his body in an iron closet with sharp teeth however the Lord saved him and many of the pagans believed. Many had tortured him to the extent that he came before seven courts; the last one was in Angora. In every time he increased in conviction and courage.

Finally he was beheaded thus he received the crown of martyrdom. A believing woman called Sophia took his body and buried him with great honor.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
05-28.title: The Martyrdom of St. Clement, Bishop of Angora

05-28.html:
Today also of the year 26 of the martyrs (310 A.D.) was the martyrdom of St. Babylas (Philyas) bishop of Thmoui (Tamai) el-Amdid. He was born to a respectable family in the city of Thmoui el-Amdid and he studied Philosophy, sciences and literature and he excelled in them. The Emperor appointed him a governor for his region.

Because of his life of piety and holiness that he lived, he forsook the governmental duties and was consecrated a bishop for the same region. He took interest in exhorting and teaching the flock, visiting and leading them in the way of holiness and steadfastness in the faith in the time of persecution.

The Saint went to Alexandria to receive the blessing of the Holy Father Pope Peter the Seal of Martyrs; there he saw the torment of the martyrs of Alexandria. He encouraged and strengthened them. The Governor seized and imprisoned him. He sent a pastoral epistle to the people of his diocese urging them to be firm in the faith and the suffering for the sake of the name of Christ to receive the joyous eternal life.

He was taken to the place of execution, he stretched his arms on the shape of a cross, prayed with a loud voice, and the soldier struck his neck with the sword thus received the crown of martyrdom.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
05-28.title: The Martyrdom of St. Babylas (Philyas) Bishop of Thmoui (Tamai) El-Amdid

05-29.html:
On this day, St. Eksani (St. Xene) departed. She was the only daughter of one of the noble families of Rome. She was raised on loving worship, reading the biography of saints and being compassionate to the poor.

She frequently visited the houses of virgins in Rome trying to follow their footsteps. The son of one of the government ministers of Rome asked to marry her. Her father prepared all the needs of her wedding. However she asked her mother to go to visit some nuns to bid them farewell.

When she allowed, she took two of her maiden servants and her precious ornaments and sailed to Cyprus where she met St. Epiphanius bishop of Cyprus. She informed him of her desire for the monastic life. He advised her to go to Alexandria. She obeyed and sailed to Alexandria where she met Pope Theophilus (23rd Patriarch)

She informed him of her desire and she handed to him all her jewels. He attached her to one of the houses of virgins. The Pope sold the jewels and built with the price a church after the name of St. Stephen in Alexandria.

Eksani persevered in practicing life of asceticism and worship for more than twenty years. When her departure drew near, a cross of light appeared in heaven surrounded by an illumined circle of stars in the middle of the day. This scene remained until her pure body was buried. The people of Alexandria realized that it was a heavenly sign indicating the eminence of her spiritual life.

The blessing of her prayers be with us all. Amen.
05-29.title: The Departure of St. Eksanie (St. Xene)

05-29.html:
On this day also St. Syriacus the struggle-mantled, departed.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
05-29.title: The Departure of St. Seriakus (Syriacus) the Struggle-mantled

05-30.html:
On this day, the holy virgins, Pistis, Helpis, Agape, and their mother Sophia were martyred. St. Sophia was from a rich and noble family in Antioch. God granted her these three daughters and she called them Pistis, which means faith, Helpis means hope, Agape means love and Sophia means wisdom.

This saint went with her three daughters to Rome to teach them the church subjects and worship. When their report reached Emperor Hadrian, he summoned them. He tried to force them to forsake the Christian faith. However their mother encouraged them to steadfast in the faith of the Lord Christ to receive the crowns of martyrdom.

Pistis was 12 years old, Helpis was 11 years old and Agape was 9 years old. When the Emperor saw their dedication to the faith, he tore Pistis body with the whips, cast her in a fiery furnace then beheaded her.

As of Helpis he combed her body with a sharp iron combs then struck her neck with the sword. When the turn of Agape the youngest came he found her firm in the faith and was not terrified from killing her two sisters before her. He ordered to cast her in the fiery furnace then crushed her in the Hinbazeen and finally beheaded her.

Their mother Sophia rejoiced exceedingly and thanked the Lord for her daughters were steadfast in the faith and that they received the crowns of martyrdom and became brides for the Lord Christ.

She took their bodies and shrouded them with expensive shrouds. She asked the Lord to receive her spirit and the Lord hearkened to her prayer and she delivered her pure spirit in the hand of the Lord. The believers took their pure bodies and buried them with great honor.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all. Amen.
05-30.title: The Martyrdom of the Virginal Saints Pistis, Helpis, Agape and their Mother Sophia

05-30.html:
On this day also of the year 492 of the martyrs (776 A.D.) Pope Mina I, the 47th Patriarch of Alexandria, departed. This Holy Father was born in the city of Samanoud and was brought up with a Christian upbringing.

When he grew he became a monk in the monastery of St. Macarius by the name of the monk Mina. After the departure of Pope Khaeil (Michael) I, the bishops and the people convened and they unanimously agreed to choose the monk Mina for his many virtues and knowledge.

After his enthronement he paid a great interest in shepherding his people and visiting them. He also built and renovated the ruined churches. A severe hardship befell him which was incited by one of the monks who desired to receive the bishopric rank by any means. The Pope faced many pressures because of this issue but he endured with patience and courage.

When he finished his good endeavor departed in peace and was buried in St. Mark church in Alexandria. He sat on the apostolic throne for 8 years and 10 months.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
05-30.title: The Departure of Pope Mina I, the 47th Patriarch of Alexandria

05-30.html:
Today also was the departure of St. Ibrahim el-Rahawy the hermit. This Holy Father was born in the city of el-Raha in Mesopotamia in the beginning of the fourth century. His parents were pious Christians and he grew in life of virtues loving the life of worship. He longed for the monastic life and asked from God often to direct his own salvation.

He dwelt in a cave in the mountain nearby his city. His family searched for him and found him in that cave. They wanted to take him with them but he refused and asked them not to visit him again. After a while he shut his cave and left a small window to receive his rations. He remained in seclusion for about fifty years and became an example for the hermits, very simple in his way of life.

There was a village nearby him inhabited by heathen wicked people and no one of the Christians could enter it to preach the name of the Lord Christ. St Jacob of Serug the bishop of the area asked St. Ibrahim the hermit to go to this village to preach its people with the name of the Lord Christ. St. Ibrahim felt a strong zeal for this mission. He left his cave and entered this village and started to call in the name of the Lord Christ. The heathen people persecuted him, beat him severely and expelled him out of the village. He remained outside the village entreating God to visit them with His mercy. God answered his prayers and moved their hearts. They went to him and he preached them with the words of life and the faith of the Lord Christ.

Some of them were touched and asked from him to forgive them for what they had done against him. They went on listening to the words of life until they believed in the name of Christ and they asked to be baptized. St. Ibrahim sent to the bishop informing him of the desire of the natives of the village. He came and baptized a large number of them. St. Ibrahim went on teaching and confirming them in the faith for a period of time. Finally he returned to his cave to resume his solitary life again.

His brother had a daughter whose name was Mariam. Her parents had died and left her alone. The devil was able to make her fall into sin. The Saint was able with the help of God to bring her back to life of repentance. She dwelt in a cave nearby his cave and practiced a good monastic life.

When St. Ibrahim finished his good endeavor departed to the Lord in peace and he was 85 years old.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
05-30.title: The Departure of St. Ibrahim el-Rahawy the Hermit
